company.name: Coalesce.io
company.industry: Data transformation SaaS for the Snowflake ecosystem

routing_rationale: Director of Infrastructure — the operational owner of cloud posture day-to-day. Drift-from-declared-baseline is the home concept of his role; it is also the literal first stage of the Transilience loop. Tight fit.

research_summary.linkedin_signal_strength: none (sales-nav URL only — no public profile signal)
research_summary.what_we_know: Director Infrastructure at a 130-person SaaS company. At this size and stage, the Director Infra typically owns IaC, the production cloud account topology, and the runbooks that the rest of the team depends on. Security execution lives here de facto when there is no named security owner.

draft.body:
The gap between IaC-declared state and actual cloud posture widens whenever the team ships fast — bounded and known at 130 people, but rarely instrumented as a continuous signal at this stage. Closing it is mostly an architectural decision: treat drift as continuous evaluation against a declared baseline rather than a quarterly audit exercise.

Transilience runs that continuously across IaC, cloud config, identity, and data-access controls — with remediation kept human-in-the-loop until the system has learned enough of the environment to expand autonomy.

Worth fifteen minutes if the framing maps to how you're thinking about it?
draft.architecture: signal-to-question — the signal is the named gap (IaC-declared vs actual), the question is whether to treat it as continuous

witness.what_works: Opening sentence names a real engineering reality (IaC drift) without flattering or fearmongering. 'Bounded and known at 130 people, but rarely instrumented as a continuous signal' gives the reader credit for already knowing the gap exists — the email is not selling them the problem. Product sentence is honest about the human-in-the-loop default. CTA is direct.
witness.what_fails: No signal-to-this-person specificity. The email could be sent to any Director of Infrastructure at a 130-person SaaS without much modification. Acceptable for a first-touch where the role-pattern is the strongest signal we have, but if a follow-up doesn't earn additional specificity, persistence will read as templating.

review_flags: low-personalization: role-pattern only, no individual signal
